take_homes: Test an agent by checking its citations to my own files. If it cites them, it read them. If not, it made things up.
Memory is a folder of plain text I own. The model underneath can change and the folder stays.
Adding a new source should make existing pages sharper, not longer. If a page looks the same after, the memory is only growing.

monday.move: Pick one live problem and put 5-8 of its documents in a folder. Have the agent build topic pages with citations, then add one new source and check whether the pages actually changed.
monday.who: me, alone, with no data that is sensitive or regulated
monday.when: Tuesday afternoon, between steering groups, if I get an hour
monday.stop_condition: If the pages don't change when I add the new source, or answers are uncited, I stop and write it off.
monday.blocker: A calendar full of the last programme's steering groups, and not knowing whether our AI policy allows connecting the wiki.

misconception.why: This one is different from the earlier programmes because I can run it myself and check the citations and the page changes. It is not proven yet. Whether it keeps compounding over months is the part I still doubt, so wait and see is still partly true.

one_line: First one of these where I could check the claim myself, but I still want to see month three.
